## Natural history notes

A small cuckoo bee characterized by a slender wasp-like body, reddish to dark markings, pale yellow patches, and relatively sparse hair compared with pollen-collecting bees. In Florida, the Fervid Nomad Bee is likely found in sunny open or semi-open habitats such as sandhills, pine flatwoods, roadsides, gardens, fields, and forest edges where spring wildflowers and ground-nesting host bees occur. Unlike bees that gather pollen for their own young, Nomada bees are cleptoparasites, with females laying eggs in the nests of other solitary bees so their larvae can use the stored pollen provisions.
